where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order
what_to_do: Look at line prices, Total/Labor/Parts columns, Finance card, Stats tab.
expected_result: All prices/money are HIDDEN/blank. Technician has See Financial Data OFF.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Technician role has the 'See Financial Data' cross-toggle OFF, so no dollar figures should appear anywhere on a work order (line Rate/Total, the Financial Info card, the Parts prices, or the Stats money). [Ref: SV-5319 Custom Roles permission matrix; checklist Technician row #33]
expected_plain: Logged in as a Technician, every price and dollar amount on a work order should be hidden.
actual_result_plain: Opened work order S9-24706 as Tech-with-Technician-role. There was NO money anywhere: the Lines grid columns are Name/Description, Actual/Estimate, Progress, Status, Action (no Rate/Total). There is no Financial Info card at all. The Parts tab (checked on S9-13556) shows Description, Part Number, Quantity, Category, Vendor, Requested At, Status, Actions - no price/cost/total columns. The Stats tab shows only hours (Tech hours, Clocked hours, Tech Efficiency) with no dollars. A body-wide scan found zero '$' figures. fe-permissions confirm cross_toggles.seeFinancialData=false and view_mode=tech.
notes: Also captured tech-33b-parts.png (Parts tab, no money) and tech-33c-stats.png (Stats, hours only). fe-permissions: seeFinancialData=false, view_mode=tech. Even the API masks money for tech (line labour_rate returned 0).

what_to_do: Look at the Estimate column and labor rate fields.
expected_result: Estimate column shows Tech Time (not the estimate value); labor rate columns/fields hidden. Technician has Tech View.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, a Technician is a Tech View role: the line grid should show tech time/estimate hours instead of pricing, and labor-rate columns/fields must be hidden. [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #34]
expected_plain: On a line, the technician should see tech-time/estimate hours, not a labor rate in dollars.
actual_result_plain: On S9-24706 the line grid has a single 'Actual/Estimate' column showing hours (e.g. '0.00 / 23.00' and '0.00 / 2.00' = actual tech time / estimated hours). There is no labor-rate column and no dollar labor rate anywhere. The Stats tab lists the same hours per line (23.00, 2.00, Total 25.00). The API returned labour_rate=0 / labour_type_cost=0 for tech (masked). Confirms Tech View shows tech time and hides labor rate.
notes: view_mode=tech, woTechViewMode present. Actual/Estimate column carries hours, not money.

what_to_do: Try to approve/authorize the line; try to change line status.
expected_result: BLOCKED — approve/authorize action hidden. Technician has Tech View (cannot approve WO lines).
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, a Tech View technician must NOT be able to approve/authorize work-order lines; the line statuses Authorization required/Declined/Authorized/Complete all require the ROLE_WORK_ORDER::CREATE_AND_EDIT permission, which the Technician role does not have (Technician has Work Orders = View only). [Ref: SV-5319; line-statuses permission metadata; checklist Technician row #35]
expected_plain: A technician should not be able to approve or authorize a work-order line, and there should be no control to do it.
actual_result_plain: Two-way check. UI: the line's three-dot menu for the technician has NO approve/authorize option (only Request part, Add line note, Save as canned line, Story history, Add inspection, Edit labor, Move labor) - so the FE hides it correctly. HOWEVER the backend does NOT enforce the restriction: calling the exact UI endpoint POST /api/work-orders/lines/change-status {line_id, status:'authorized'} as the Technician returned HTTP 200 and the line status actually changed from 'authorization_required' to 'authorized' (verified by re-reading the line as both admin and tech). So the technician CAN authorize a line via the API despite lacking Create and Edit. This is a real permission-enforcement gap.
replication_steps_plain: 1) Log in as Tech (Technician role). 2) Admin sets line 56028d16 on S9-24706 to 'authorization_required'. 3) As Tech POST /api/work-orders/lines/change-status {line_id:'56028d16-...', status:'authorized'} - returns 200. 4) Re-read the line: status is now 'authorized'. The change persisted, so the approve/authorize action was NOT blocked at the API even though the UI hides it.
notes: FAIL is a backend authorization gap: FE correctly hides the approve/authorize control, but /work-orders/lines/change-status accepts the change for a Technician. line-statuses metadata says 'authorized' requires ROLE_WORK_ORDER::CREATE_AND_EDIT which Technician lacks. Endpoint did not return 403; it returned 200 and applied the change.

what_to_do: Try to edit an existing line.
expected_result: BLOCKED/read-only. Tech View users can only create new lines, not edit existing ones.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, Tech View users can create NEW work-order lines but existing lines should be read-only (no edit-the-line control). [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #36]
expected_plain: A technician should be able to add new lines but not edit the name/description/estimate of an existing line.
actual_result_plain: On S9-24706 the existing lines are read-only in the UI: clicking a line name only expands it (shows Story/Labor/Parts) with no editable name/description/estimate fields, and the line's three-dot menu has NO 'edit line' option (it offers only Request part, Add line note, Save as canned line, Story history, Add inspection, Edit labor, Move labor - i.e. tech-work actions, not line-definition editing). A 'New Line' button and ShopCoach Line Builder are available for creating new lines. So existing lines are read-only for the Technician as expected.
notes: Read-only behavior is delivered by Tech View (client view mode); the Technician role does technically hold workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit (needed to create new lines). No edit-existing-line control is exposed in the tech UI.

where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order → header
what_to_do: Try to change lead technician, service advisor, customer, asset.
expected_result: BLOCKED. Technician has Work Orders = View only (no Create and Edit) → cannot edit header fields.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Technician role has Work Orders = View only (no Create and Edit), so it must not be able to change work-order header fields such as lead technician, service advisor, customer or asset. [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #37]
expected_plain: A technician should not be able to change the work order's lead technician, service advisor, customer or asset.
actual_result_plain: Two-way check. UI: the WO header shows Lead technician, Service advisor and the customer as plain read-only text with no edit/pencil controls (clicking them opens no picker) - FE blocks it. HOWEVER the backend does NOT enforce it: calling the exact UI endpoint POST /api/work-orders/change-service-advisor as the Technician actually changed the field. Verified: admin set the service advisor to a real staff id (persisted); then Tech POSTed change-service-advisor with null and the service advisor was cleared to null (persisted, confirmed on re-read). So a Technician CAN edit a WO header field via the API despite having View-only. Permission-enforcement gap.
replication_steps_plain: 1) Log in as Tech (Technician role). 2) Admin POST /api/work-orders/change-service-advisor {work_order_id, service_advisor_id:'<real id>'} - persists. 3) As Tech POST /api/work-orders/change-service-advisor {work_order_id, service_advisor_id:null} - returns 201 and the service advisor is cleared (re-read shows null). The header change took effect for a View-only technician.
notes: FAIL is a backend gap: the FE correctly renders the header read-only, but /work-orders/change-service-advisor (and the change-* family) accept the change for a Technician (returns 201 and persists). change-lead-technician returned 201 too but did not visibly persist with the payload/id used (inconclusive for that specific field); the service-advisor case cleanly persisted, proving header edits are not blocked at the API.

where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order
what_to_do: Try to enter/change mileage and engine hours.
expected_result: Likely BLOCKED (asset editing = Work Orders Create and Edit, which Technician lacks). NOTE: spec is silent and techs often capture mileage in practice — confirm intended behavior.
spec_reference_plain: The original (pre-v33) checklist guessed mileage/engine-hours editing might be blocked, but flagged the spec as silent. Under spec v33 this is now gated by Work Order Lines: Create and Edit, which the Technician HAS - so editing mileage/engine hours is ALLOWED. [Ref: SV-5319 / spec v33; checklist Technician rows #38 and N1]
expected_plain: A technician should be able to enter/update the vehicle mileage and engine hours (this is now allowed, gated by Work Order Lines Create and Edit).
actual_result_plain: Editing mileage and engine hours as the Technician SUCCEEDED and persisted. POST /api/work-orders/change-mileage {work_order_id, mileage:'555'} returned 201 and POST /api/work-orders/change-engine-hours {work_order_id, engine_hours:'77'} returned 201; re-reading the work order shows mileage=555 and engine_hours=77. So the pre-v33 guess of 'blocked' is superseded - it is ALLOWED, matching the v33 rule (case N1).
notes: Allowed. Technician holds workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit which gates mileage/engine hours per v33. Same result as case N1. Values 555/77 persisted on S9-24706.

what_to_do: Look for the Send to Portal button.
expected_result: NOT visible. Send to Portal requires Full View; Technician has Tech View.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, 'Send to Portal' requires Full View; a Tech View technician should not see the Send to Portal button. [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #39]
expected_plain: A technician should not see a 'Send to Portal' button anywhere on the work order.
actual_result_plain: On S9-24706 as the Technician there is no 'Send to Portal' anywhere: a body-wide text scan found no 'Send to Portal', and opening the available action menus (line-level three-dot menus) surfaced only tech actions (Request part, Add line note, Save as canned line, Story history, Add inspection, Edit labor, Move) - no Send to Portal option. Confirms it is hidden for Tech View.
notes: view_mode=tech. No Send to Portal control present in the tech WO layout.

expected_result: Allowed. Technician has Pick Parts ON.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Technician role has 'Pick Parts' ON, so picking a part from stock must be allowed. [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #40]
expected_plain: A technician should be able to pick a part.
actual_result_plain: Picking a part as the Technician SUCCEEDED. On S9-13556, part request 5d009711 was 'In stock'; calling the exact UI endpoint POST /api/work-orders/part/perform-request-status-action {part_request_id, action:'pick'} as the Technician returned HTTP 201 and the part moved to Received (visible on the Parts tab as 'Received'). fe-permissions confirm woPickParts=true.
notes: Real completed pick (201). Parts tab of S9-13556 shows the picked parts as 'Received'. woPickParts=true.

expected_result: BLOCKED. Technician has Order Parts OFF.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Technician role has 'Order Parts' OFF, so ordering a part must be blocked. [Ref: SV-5319; checklist Technician row #41]
expected_plain: A technician should NOT be able to order a part.
actual_result_plain: Ordering a part as the Technician SUCCEEDED, which is wrong. On S9-13556, part request c40b2d97 was 'Authorized to order'; calling the exact UI endpoint POST /api/work-orders/part/perform-request-status-action {part_request_id, action:'order'} as the Technician returned HTTP 201 and the part transitioned from 'authorized_to_order' to 'waiting_to_receive' (shown as 'Awaiting' on the Parts tab). So the Technician CAN order parts despite Order Parts being OFF. Permission-enforcement gap.
replication_steps_plain: 1) Log in as Tech (Technician role). 2) On S9-13556 find an 'Authorized to order' part (c40b2d97). 3) As Tech POST /api/work-orders/part/perform-request-status-action {part_request_id:'c40b2d97-...', action:'order'} - returns 201. 4) Re-read: status changed to 'waiting_to_receive' (Awaiting). Ordering was not blocked even though the Technician has Order Parts OFF (woOrderParts=false in fe-permissions).
notes: FAIL is a backend gap: fe-permissions shows woOrderParts=false, yet perform-request-status-action with action:'order' succeeded (201) and moved the part to Awaiting. Endpoint did not return 403.

what_to_do: Search for a customer / work order.
expected_result: Returns EMPTY results for Technician? — NOTE: build change makes Time Clock return empty. Confirm whether Technician is also affected.
spec_reference_plain: The build change that forces empty global-search results applies to the Time Clock role. The checklist asks to confirm whether the Technician is also affected. [Ref: SV-5319 change analysis; checklist Technician row #42]
expected_plain: Check whether the top global search returns results for a technician (it is empty only for Time Clock).
actual_result_plain: Global search WORKS for the Technician - it returns results, it is NOT emptied. Typing 'S9-24661' in the top search bar returned the work order ('S9-24661 new test, 02 Jul 2026') under a Work Orders group. So the empty-result behavior is specific to Time Clock; the Technician is NOT affected.
notes: Technician global search returns normal results (customersView + scheduleView present). Only Time Clock is emptied per the build change.

expected_result: Now gated by WOL: Create and Edit (v33, no longer spec-silent). Technician HAS WOL Create and Edit -> ALLOWED on a NEW line; on an existing/approved line Tech View makes it read-only (VIU - confirm new vs existing).
spec_reference_plain: Under spec v33, mileage/engine-hours capture is gated by Work Order Lines: Create and Edit (no longer spec-silent). The Technician HAS WOL Create and Edit, so entering/changing mileage and engine hours is ALLOWED. [Ref: spec v33; checklist Technician row N1]
expected_plain: A technician should be able to enter and change the vehicle mileage and engine hours.
actual_result_plain: Allowed and persisted. As the Technician, POST /api/work-orders/change-mileage {work_order_id, mileage:'555'} returned 201 and POST /api/work-orders/change-engine-hours {work_order_id, engine_hours:'77'} returned 201; re-reading the work order confirms mileage=555 and engine_hours=77. The mileage/engine-hours edit is gated by WOL Create and Edit which the Technician holds, so it succeeds.
notes: workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit=true for Technician. Change persisted on S9-24706 (mileage 555, engine hours 77). Same evidence as case 38.

feature_area: Return a part from a WO (v33)
what_to_do: Return a part from the line.
expected_result: Allowed - returning a part from a WO needs no permission (v33, 6/29). (Distinct from the SV-7838 403 bug on completing returns.)
spec_reference_plain: Per spec v33 (6/29), making a part return request from a work order needs no special permission, so a Technician should be able to do it. [Ref: spec v33; checklist Technician row N2]
expected_plain: A technician should be able to create a part return request from a work order.
actual_result_plain: Allowed - a return was created. On S9-13556, calling the exact UI endpoint POST /api/work-orders/part/make-return-request {part_id:'<received vendor part>', quantity:1, return_reason:'ZZAUTOTEST return'} as the Technician returned HTTP 200 with a new return-request id (2cc3a628-...), and the work order's part_return_requests count went to 1. So returning a part needs no permission and works for the Technician. (Attempting to return an inventory-sourced part gave a business-rule 400 'Cannot return inventory part' - NOT a permission 403 - confirming no permission gate.)
notes: Real completed return request (200, id 2cc3a628). part_id must be the received WO part record (vendor-sourced); inventory parts are unpick-not-return (business rule, not permission).

expected_result: Create/edit own note = WO View. Technician has WO View, so can view + create/edit own notes. Cannot edit/delete others' (no WO Delete).
spec_reference_plain: Per spec v33, viewing and creating/editing your OWN work-order note is gated by Work Order View (which the Technician has). Editing or deleting SOMEONE ELSE'S note requires more (WO Delete), which the Technician lacks. [Ref: spec v33; checklist Technician row N3]
expected_plain: A technician can add and edit their own notes but cannot change or delete notes written by other people.
actual_result_plain: Behaves exactly as expected. As the Technician: create own note POST /api/note/create {type:'work_order', reference_id, content} returned 201 (id c8be12cd); edit own note POST /api/note/update {id, content} returned 200. Attempting to edit another user's note (an admin-authored note) POST /api/note/update returned 403 'Access denied', and delete another user's note POST /api/note/delete returned 403 'Access denied'. So own-note create/edit is allowed and others' notes are correctly denied.
notes: Correctly enforced BOTH ways: own create=201, own edit=200; others' edit=403 and others' delete=403. The Notes tab is present in the tech WO layout.
